title: Thonburi Kingdom
capsule: The Thonburi Kingdom was founded in late 1767 by Taksin, a general of Teochew Chinese descent, after Burmese forces of the Konbaung dynasty sacked and burned Ayutthaya in April 1767, killing or deporting much of the population. Operating from the west bank of the Chao Phraya opposite present-day Bangkok, Taksin reunified the fragmented Siamese polities within four years, then extended influence over Lan Na, Vientiane, Luang Prabang, and Cambodia. His later reign was marked by mental instability and a controversial claim to be a Buddhist saint; he was deposed in a coup on 6 April 1782. His military commander Chao Phraya Chakri was recalled from a Cambodian campaign, assumed the throne as Rama I, founded the Chakri dynasty, and shifted the capital across the river to Bangkok.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The kingdom's core territory in the Chao Phraya basin is well-attested; outer tributary zones — especially Cambodia and the Laotian principalities — represent spheres of influence rather than administered territory, and the precise polygon boundaries are uncertain.
